1	# JusPrin production architecture
2	
3	**Status:** This is the architecture chosen for the `jusprin-newui` branch. It also says where production code may and may not reach into OrcaSlicer.
4	
5	JusPrin replaces what OrcaSlicer looks like and how people move through it. It keeps everything OrcaSlicer already does well to turn a model into a print. Product work should make it easier for people to say what they want and to check a print before sending it. It must not create JusPrin's own version of slicing, geometry, rendering, picking (working out which object the pointer is on), saving and loading, or undo history.
6	
7	## Product composition
8	
9	The project window we are building toward has four regions that stay in place:
10	
11	1. A compact row that shows the printer and the project status.
12	2. A thin pane that lists plates and objects and can be collapsed.
13	3. OrcaSlicer's existing Prepare canvas (the 3D view).
14	4. A fixed pane that holds the Agent conversation and the print plan.
15	
16	The compact plates/objects pane is deferred to a later task. The first
17	production shell and the first Agent implementation must not depend on it.
18	Until the pane is added, people work with objects through the native canvas
19	and the Agent.
20	
21	Prepare is the screen people stay on. **Check print** opens a modal window. That window holds a second copy of OrcaSlicer's real Preview widget and shows the current valid slice of the active plate. OrcaSlicer's original Preview stays where it was, in `Plater`'s Notebook (OrcaSlicer's tabbed container). A small factory function on `Plater`, with nothing JusPrin-specific in it, gives that window the existing model, bed, slicing process, and G-code result. Closing the window returns focus to Prepare. The window also closes by itself when the project or the slice changes. **Print** currently opens OrcaSlicer's existing send confirmation dialog. It never sends straight away. Project details open as a drawer. Monitor is a separate screen that can stay visible while the person does other work.
22	
23	## Runtime architecture
24	
25	```text
26	OrcaSlicer process (C++17 / wxWidgets / OpenGL)
27	├── JusPrin application shell
28	│   ├── compact top navigation and machine status
29	│   ├── native plates/objects pane
30	│   ├── center workspace host
31	│   │   └── existing GLCanvas3D Prepare canvas
32	│   └── wxWebView
33	│       └── local React/TypeScript Agent interface
34	├── modal Check print window with Orca G-code Preview
35	├── typed workspace/controller boundary
36	├── existing Orca model, selection, plates, gizmos, and undo stack
37	└── existing slicing, project I/O, device, and print subsystems
38	```
39	
40	The split between native code and web code is deliberately cautious:
41	
42	- The 3D view, and anything drawn on top of it, stays native.
43	- The top row and the object/plate pane start as native wxWidgets.
44	- C++ owns the application state and the project state.
45	- The WebView receives versioned events and sends versioned commands.
46	- We may later try building the object pane in a WebView, but only as a change to how that one pane is drawn. It would not be a reason to move to Electron or to a WebGL 3D view.
47	
48	## Authoritative ownership
49	
50	For each kind of state, one part of the system holds the real copy. This table says which part, and what JusPrin does with that state.
51	
52	| Concern | Authoritative owner | JusPrin responsibility |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| Project model and object identity | Orca `Model` and `ObjectID` | Show a typed view that is valid only for the current project session |
55	| Plates and active plate | Orca `PartPlateList` | Show them, and ask for changes through commands |
56	| Selection and picking | Orca `Selection` and `GLCanvas3D` | Keep the UI in sync without creating feedback loops |
57	| Geometry transforms | Orca gizmos and `GizmoObjectManipulation` | Start the existing behavior and show exact values |
58	| Undo and redo | Orca undo stack | Report whether undo and redo are available and what they did. Keep no second undo stack |
59	| Slicing and Preview | Orca slicing actions and Preview canvas | Show the states of Slice and Check print |
60	| Project serialization | Orca 3MF and model serializers | Keep files compatible. Add migration only for new data |
61	| Agent conversation | React/TypeScript WebView | Render messages, write the words people and the model read, and submit typed commands (see [Where logic goes](#where-logic-goes-the-page-first)) |
62	| Agent print plan | C++/agent application boundary | Explain intent, decisions, uncertainty, and consequences |
63	
64	## Production integration boundaries
65	
66	### Shell host
67	
68	The shell is the JusPrin window frame around OrcaSlicer's content. Build one shell, in files this fork owns, and attach it to `MainFrame` in one small place. Decisions about what happens at startup go in a bootstrap or a shell factory that the fork owns. Do not spread environment checks through OrcaSlicer's constructors.
69	
70	The first production version may still construct OrcaSlicer's old top bar, tab panel, Sidebar, and `GUI_ObjectList` where existing OrcaSlicer behavior depends on them. Leave them out of the visible layout. Do not hide them behind a separate top-level window. Stopping them from being constructed at all is a separate project, because it changes object lifetimes.
71	
72	### Build registration
73	
74	List JusPrin's source files explicitly in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake`. OrcaSlicer's central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt` should pull that file in with one include line that never changes. The fork should not keep adding its own files to OrcaSlicer's list.
75	
76	### Workspace boundary
77	
78	The workspace API is the typed C++ interface JusPrin uses to read and change the project. The production version should keep the ideas from the proof of concept (POC) that worked:
79	
80	- separate types for plate IDs and object IDs, so one cannot be passed where the other is expected;
81	- read-only snapshots of the project;
82	- explicit errors from commands;
83	- typed reasons that say what kind of change happened;
84	- a revision number that only goes up;
85	- subscriptions that end automatically when the object holding them is destroyed, and that can be moved but not copied.
86	
87	Before production use, the API must also:
88	
89	- say which calls must run on the GUI thread;
90	- say exactly when the revision number goes up;
91	- explicitly mark the old session's IDs invalid when a project is replaced;
92	- notice changes that did not go through the adapter (the JusPrin class that implements this API on top of OrcaSlicer);
93	- report undo and redo availability whether or not any particular widget is visible;
94	- report whether an undo or redo really changed OrcaSlicer's state;
95	- not depend on `GUI_ObjectList` for commands that change the model;
96	- offer plate selection, object import and addition, and the other commands the product needs;
97	- keep wxWidgets types and OrcaSlicer types out of its public interface.
98	
99	Sometimes the operation you need exists only inside OrcaSlicer's UI code. In that case, add the smallest possible command to the OrcaSlicer class that already does the work, and name it for what it does. Do not copy the operation into JusPrin. Do not fake clicks or key presses on hidden controls.
100	
101	### Canvas presentation
102	
103	`GLCanvas3D` keeps a small API for controlling how its parts are presented. That API contains nothing specific to JusPrin. A controller in fork-owned code uses the API to apply JusPrin's choices, and puts OrcaSlicer's previous state back when the controller is destroyed. Whether a control is drawn and whether it receives input must be two separate switches. Otherwise a control that is hidden could still swallow pointer events. OrcaSlicer's native gizmos (the on-canvas tools such as Move and Rotate) must stay usable while one is active.
104	
105	The Check print window's preview has its own controller, `PreviewPresentationController` beside `CanvasPresentationController`. It hides the canvas's legacy overlay layer (plate selector strip, 3D navigator, canvas toolbar), holds OrcaSlicer's app-wide G-code listing preference (`show_gcode_window`) off while the window is open, and switches the legend through `GCodeViewer::show_legend`; destroying it restores all three, on every close path. Both sliders stay as OrcaSlicer draws them. OrcaSlicer's single ImGui context also keeps the last pointer position of whichever canvas saw it, so the window clears it when it opens and when the pointer leaves its canvas.
106	
107	The POC had one broad switch, `render_overlays`. Production needs finer control. Treat each of these as its own item that can be shown or hidden separately: OrcaSlicer's main toolbar, the gizmo picker, the handles of the active gizmo, plate actions, object labels, layer-editing controls, navigation aids, the Preview legend, and the Preview sliders. Some controls are shared between canvases, such as `Plater`'s collapse toolbar. A shared control must be saved and restored by one object that lives as long as the shell does. Do not give each canvas its own guard for it.
108	
109	### Plates and Project pane
110	
111	This pane is native code owned by the fork (`Shell/LeftPane`). It sits to the left of the workspace on Prepare. Its first tab lists every plate, even when the project has only one. Its second tab shows the saved project's identity, the model's 3MF metadata, the history of physical prints, the version history, and export. The pane keeps no project state of its own and has no undo of its own. It draws what two model classes describe, and those classes do not depend on the GUI. Every click calls a workspace command.
112	
113	| Piece | What it is responsible for |
114	|---|---|
115	| `Workspace/ProjectOutline.hpp`, `IWorkspace::outline()` | The data the pane reads: plates, copies of objects (each with the plate that holds it), volumes, facts about customization and the mesh, and what is selected below the object level. Which plate a copy is on comes from `PartPlateList`. The code never guesses it from where the copy sits. |
116	| `Shell/LeftPaneModel` | Which rows the Plates tab shows, and when. The active plate is open. Other plates are folded, each with a summary computed from its current copies. A row has child rows only when there is data for them. "Not on a plate" appears only when some copy is on no plate. This class also handles switching between the tabs and between the views inside the Project tab. |
117	| `Shell/ProjectPaneModel` | The contents of the Details view, as plain data. A field that nobody filled in is left out. The project's print history is one row on the Project tab's root that opens the Print history screen. |
118	| `Workspace/OrcaOutline.cpp` | The commands, implemented on top of OrcaSlicer: `select_plate`, `add_plate`, `select_copy`, `select_volume`, `plate_actions`, `run_plate_action`. Each command ends by calling the same code OrcaSlicer's own UI calls (`Plater::select_plate_by_hover_id`, the toolbar's Add plate event, `Selection` plus the canvas's object-select event). The events are raised synchronously on the GUI thread, so the change has already happened when the command returns. |
119	| `Shell/LeftPane`, `LeftPaneProject.cpp` | Drawing and input. While drawing, the pane records where each control ended up. Pointer handling looks each click up in that record, so a click can only hit something that was actually drawn. |
120	
121	The ledger is the project's G-code records (`Agent/ManufacturingHistory.hpp`): one record per G-code that left the project, keyed by the SHA-256 of the plate's sliced G-code, holding where it went (exports, sends) and the prints the printer reported (started, finished; never a failure). Slicing writes nothing. It can have any number of subscribers, through `ProjectPersistence::subscribe_ledger`. The pane and the header's overflow menu each subscribe to it separately.
122	
123	`Shell/GcodeHistoryRecorder` writes the records where OrcaSlicer already says a file left: `EVT_OUTPUT_EXPORTED` for an export (OrcaSlicer's own and the `export_file` tool's), the Bambu print and send jobs' finished events while their dialog is showing, and the print-host queue's enqueue observer followed by the queue dialog's progress at 100. Each time, a copy of the G-code is kept at `<project>/gcode/<hash>.gcode` (the last `kKeptGcodeCopies` per project). It polls Bambu printers every two seconds whatever is on screen; `Agent/PrintOutcomeTracker` decides which report belongs to which send, and a finish of a project that is not open is written into that project's saved document. Print-host printers record sends only. The model reads the last ten records as `printHistory` in its workspace block.
124	
125	The records are shown on one screen, Print history, the second screen of the Home page (`HomeUI/src/components/PrintHistory.tsx`). It is a leaf of Home and of the project: the gallery's header link, a project card's or printer card's history line, the project pane's Print history row and a chat marker's "history" link all open it, and where it was opened from sets its first filter. Back from the gallery stays in the page; opened from the project, the shell selects Home with the screen named (`ShellController::open_print_history`, sent as the `screen` message when Home comes on screen) and Back selects the tab it came from. The page asks for the entries (`history_request`) each time it opens and each time the host's state moves under it; `Home/PrintHistory` builds them from every project's records, pure and tested in `agent_bridge_tests`, with what only the application knows (preset labels, which printer card a printer is, the exported files' checks) passed in by `OrcaHomeBackend`. An exported file is hashed again when the screen asks, unless its size and time are as they were at the last hash. Export… writes the project's kept copy and records it; Export again on a changed file writes a new file beside it. Open in chat opens the project if another is open and asks the Agent page to show the chat and scroll to the marker (`reveal_item`). The page phrases every line; nothing records, badges or draws a failure.
126	
127	Print again sends a recorded G-code's kept file, never a fresh slice, and always through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog, where the person presses Send. A Bambu printer takes a `.gcode.3mf`, so a Bambu print also keeps the package it uploaded (`<hash>.gcode.3mf`, and for a cloud printer the config 3MF it also sent), byte for byte, with its SHA-256 on the send (`packageHash`); it goes when its G-code's copy is pruned. Print again parses that package, hands it to Select Machine through `Plater::update_print_required_data` and `EVT_PRINT_FROM_SDCARD_VIEW` (the printer file browser's print-from-storage mode, which draws the plate, picture and filaments from the file), and sets the dialog's new-print flag (`SelectMachineDialog::set_required_data_new_print`, the one upstream seam), so the job uploads the local file as a new print instead of asking the printer to print by name. Printing from the printer's storage is not used: the file name on the printer is reused per project, so it cannot say which version would print. A print host with OrcaSlicer's standard upload dialog is sent a temporary copy of the kept G-code (the queue deletes what it uploads); ElegooLink, Creality Print, Flashforge's local API and `use_3mf` hosts are not offered Print again. `GcodeHistoryRecorder::print_again_state` decides whether it is offered for the printer selected now; a kept file whose hash no longer matches is never sent and the entry says so. `print_dialog_open` opens the same dialogs for the agent: a plate's slice, or with `gcode` a recorded G-code.
128	
129	### Opening and importing files
130	
131	Decided 2026-10-24. A file reaches JusPrin in a handful of ways, and they mean one of two things: **start from this file**, or **add this to the project I am working on**. The first is what a person means almost every time they bring a file in; the second is the minority case (a multi-part print), and the person signals it by aiming at the plate or by asking the agent. Because autosave keeps every project, starting a new project by mistake costs one click on Recent, while adding to the wrong project leaves a stray part in it. So every way in starts a new project unless the person aimed at the plate.
132	
133	| How the file is opened | Model file (STL, STEP, OBJ, AMF, …) | .3mf |
134	|---|---|---|
135	| Opened from the OS: a double-click in Finder or Explorer, "Open with", a browser's "open in JusPrin" | New project, named after the file; the app goes to Prepare | New project; the "Previously opened file" question if the file was opened before |
136	| Dropped on Home | Same | Same |
137	| Home's **Open…** button, File › Open Project (Cmd+O) | Same | Same |
138	| Dropped on the Prepare canvas | Added to the open project | New project, as above. OrcaSlicer's "open as project or import geometry?" question is not asked |
139	| **+ Add model** in the Plates and Project pane, File › Import (Cmd+I) | Added to the open project | Its geometry is added to the open project, without its settings (OrcaSlicer's Import) |
140	| The Agent composer's + › 3D model, a drop on the Agent pane, or a request in the chat | Attached; the agent adds it to the open project (`object_import`) | Same |
141	
142	Rules that follow from the table:
143	
144	- A model file never silently lands in whatever project happened to be open behind Home. Before 2026-10-24 Home's Import button did exactly that, because it called OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, and from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-28 the most recent project reopened behind Home at startup. Home now starts with a blank project behind it, but whatever is open there is still not where a file opened from Home goes.
145	- A file opened from the OS lands in the running JusPrin. OrcaSlicer's default starts a second process for a .3mf; JusPrin runs as a single instance on every platform.
146	- Several files opened or dropped together make one new project holding all of them.
147	- Opening a .3mf as a project is the only thing a .3mf does on the Prepare canvas. Wanting only the geometry out of a .3mf is rare, and the agent or File › Import can do it on request. The one question JusPrin asks on a file open stays the "Previously opened file" question described in the [autosave document](autosave-version-history.md).
148	- Home's primary action is **Open…**, not Import: there is nothing on Home to import into. The whole Home page accepts a dropped file, and its empty state says so ("Drop a model or project here, or Open…"). Beside it, **New** is the design system's compact outlined button (`secondarySmall`, 28 DIP) for a blank project built up part by part, quiet enough not to compete with Open; File › New Project does the same.
149	- G-code files keep OrcaSlicer's behavior (the G-code viewer) for now.
150	- In the chat, a load that started a new project draws one quiet line, "Opened bracket.3mf as a new project · you · 10:42" (the page's `MessageList`, from the file report's `projectOpened`); an import into the open project draws nothing, since the timeline's step rows already say what was added. With no agent the same report draws the "Notes about this file" card instead.
151	
152	**Finding the way to add a part.** With Home's button named Open, the person who wants a second part in the project they have needs to find it from Prepare. Every slicer solves this the same way, with a control inside the workspace that is always on screen: PrusaSlicer's Add button on the top toolbar and Cmd+I, Cura's folder icon at the top left of Prepare, and OrcaSlicer's own Add button on the main toolbar, which JusPrin hides. Dragging onto the plate is in addition to that control in all three, never the only way. JusPrin keeps the same shape: a **+ Add model** button under the plate list in the Plates tab of the Plates and Project pane, drawn like **+ Add plate** and placed directly above it, so the two things that can be added there sit together with the commoner one first (chosen on 2026-10-24 from a drawn comparison against a plus in the tab header and a row under the open plate), plus File › Import (Cmd+I), the composer's + menu, and the empty plate's hint ("Drop a model here or add one"). A person who asks the agent to add a file gets it added as well.
153	
154	Ownership: the policy is fork-owned (the Home backend, the shell's file handler and the Prepare canvas's drop target, the Plates pane's button). OrcaSlicer keeps its file dialogs, its loading code and its "Previously opened file" seam; the fork adds one seam, `Plater::set_external_file_open_handler`, that lets it take the files handed to `Plater::load_files(wxArrayString)` (the OS, another instance, the command line, a download, a drop) before OrcaSlicer adds them to the open project, and sets two of OrcaSlicer's own settings (`single_instance`, `project_load_behaviour`) to the values the table needs.
155	
156	How the paths come out of that one seam:
157	
158	- The shell's handler (`ShellController::take_opened_files`) leaves a .3mf to OrcaSlicer, which opens it as a project through `load_project` and so asks the "Previously opened file" question; files given with it are added to that project. Any other files are opened in a new project named after the first one: the open project is saved and released the way the agent's `project_open` releases it, then OrcaSlicer's own load runs into the new project, and the app goes to Prepare.
159	- A drop on the Prepare canvas must add, so the shell replaces OrcaSlicer's `PlaterDropTarget` with its own, which loads through the same call while telling the handler to stand aside. OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own target after every slice; the shell puts its own back on the next idle turn. OrcaSlicer's one-SVG emboss on drop is not kept (the shell hides that gizmo); a dropped SVG loads as an object.
160	- File › Import › Import Zip Archive also reaches `load_files(wxArrayString)`, so a zip on its own keeps OrcaSlicer's behavior and adds. Home's Open… and a drop on Home open a zip in a new project like any model file.
161	- A file dropped on Home reaches the app as its name and bytes, not its path: the web view takes the drop. On macOS a native drop target on the web view would not see it: wxWidgets 3.3 gives its WebKit view none of the drag methods it gives its own views, so WebKit's own handling runs (read from the wxWidgets source on 2026-10-24; not yet tried with a real drag). The bytes are written to `JusPrin-dropped/<MD5>/<name>` under the system temp folder and opened from there, so the "Previously opened file" question recognizes a .3mf dropped on Home before, but not one first opened from its own folder.
162	- The agent's tools load through the vector overload of `load_files` and `load_project`, which the seam does not see, and the handler stands aside while a tool's load runs.
163	- A 3MF saved for another printer keeps that printer: OrcaSlicer selects the file's system printer profile (a P1S, say) and draws its bed, the person's own printer is not re-selected, and the file's process and filament settings stay as the designer saved them. The header's printer chip is marked "from the file" while the selected profile is not a named printer (decided 2026-10-28, see the design system's Header chip); the agent's load report carries the change (`selectedSetupChange.printerPreset`) and its first message asks which printer to use. OrcaSlicer's "sync the printer information?" question is answered No on every open, since the app stores that answer at startup.
164	
165	### Print issues and OrcaSlicer's notifications
166	
167	Inside the shell OrcaSlicer's own notifications are held but not drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds: print problems as a status pill in the canvas's lower right corner, the list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is about, with **Ask AI**; the outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused) as a short confirmation above the pill; and work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export) as an entry in the chat.
168	
169	**OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth.** A notification carries a kind, a level and words. It does not carry the object it is about, so where OrcaSlicer lets its check be asked again, that check is asked once more for the object only.
170	
171	| Piece | Owns |
172	|---|---|
173	| `PrintIssues/NoticeKinds` | Where each of OrcaSlicer's notification kinds goes: the issue list, a confirmation, running work, application state, or nowhere. Every kind is named; a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in this file until someone routes it. |
174	| `PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor` | Reads the list on the notification manager's own turn, compares it with what it saw last, and rebuilds only on a change. Asks OrcaSlicer's checks for the object behind a validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an object out of a nozzle's reach and a slicing step warning. Holds no rule about what a problem is. |
175	| `issues_from` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue` | The rule, as plain data with its own tests: an object lookup's entry exists only while OrcaSlicer holds a notification of its kind; a print-problem notification no lookup answers for is a plate-wide issue in OrcaSlicer's words. |
176	| `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout`, `IssueOverlay` | Where the pieces go, how they are drawn and how they close, with ImGui inside the canvas's frame through the same overlay hook as the tool strip. The bubble never covers its object, the pill, a confirmation or the tool strip. |
177	| `PrintIssues/WorkFeed` | Work as it starts, moves on and ends. A slice is followed through OrcaSlicer's own events, which carry a percentage and an outcome. Other work is read from the "still running" notifications, which carry neither. |
178	| `AgentHost::begin_work`, `update_work`, `finish_work`; `WorkCard` in the page | The entry in the chat: saved with the project at the place in the timeline where the work started, so a later message reads below it; a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel while it runs; completed in place. The chat panel opens when work starts. Repeats are folded by the page, never in what is saved, and an entry still "running" in a project that was closed mid-run reads as interrupted. |
179	| `PrintIssues/IssueContext`, `AgentHost::submit_issue_message` | The chat message a button sends, and the one way a message enters the chat from outside the page. |
180	
181	Two things are read whether or not a notification exists, because OrcaSlicer's notifications do not cover them in time:
182	
183	- **The slice result.** A path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach, and a filament that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when OrcaSlicer's preview loads the slice, which here means opening Check print. OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the moment the slice ends.
184	- **Why a slice failed.** A critical failure is shown in a dialog and leaves no notification, and no notification says which object the failure named. `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` is the only place both exist.
185	
186	Rules that follow:
187	
188	- **No pill is the all-clear, and it is never given before a check.** The pill is drawn only while OrcaSlicer reports an issue, ignored ones included. While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the last issues are kept, the pill says it is checking and both buttons are off, so the pill does not go until OrcaSlicer has looked. An issue that was not in the list before is announced once by a ring that spreads from the pill twice; an edit that keeps an issue, and ignoring one or undoing that, announce nothing.
189	- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
190	- **"Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's answer.** An error-level notification blocks. For the slice result it is OrcaSlicer's own post-slice check, which allows a path 2 mm past the plate edge; the monitor does not apply a stricter test of its own.
191	- **The object is never read out of the words.** Two messages of one kind are told apart by comparing OrcaSlicer's words now with its words before, as OrcaSlicer does itself. Which object a message is about always comes from a check's own ids.
192	- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **One button, one question**: Ask AI sends "Explain this issue and my options." with the issue as context, and the turn gets the ordinary tools, so the person asks for a fix in the chat. A second "Resolve with AI" button was removed on 2026-10-28: it sent the same context with the same tools and differed only in the sentence, which the person could not tell apart.
193	- **Slice-result warnings follow OrcaSlicer's send dialog.** The warnings the G-code processor stores on a slice result (bed temperature, nozzle hardness, timelapse) are shown as OrcaSlicer's Bambu send dialog shows them, the only place OrcaSlicer itself shows them: never the bed-temperature one, the traditional-timelapse one once although it is stored twice. The chip and `slice_report` read one fork-owned table, `Workspace/SliceResultWarnings`, whose comment says why it is a copy and not an upstream seam, and a guard test fails when OrcaSlicer defines a kind the table does not classify. The timelapse ones apply only to a print that records a timelapse, which is chosen when it is sent: `slice_report` and Check print list them marked so, and the chip does not count them.
194	- **Operation failures are not print issues.** A failed download or a refused arrange is a confirmation, never an entry in the issue list.
195	- **Closing hides, it never resolves.** The pill is always there and is the way back; the list and the bubble are opened and closed, one at a time, and closing either changes nothing about the issue or the count. The list closes on a pick, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. Turning the view or dragging the object leaves it open. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on **Ask AI** that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the pill opens the bubble directly, and with several the bubble's pager walks them all. The overlay hears Escape and presses through handlers of its own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.
196	- **Ignoring a warning is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's.** **Ignore this warning** in the bubble leaves OrcaSlicer's notification alone: the warning stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the pill stops counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left, never "No print issues"). Only a warning can be ignored; a blocker cannot, because OrcaSlicer would still refuse to print. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that warning on the active plate's own list, and is forgotten when OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not saved with the project. The rule is `mark_ignored` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue`.
197	
198	Known limits: application and account notifications (update available, plug-in missing, preset sync conflict) are routed to `App` and drawn nowhere yet. A confirmation shows OrcaSlicer's words and a close button; the actions OrcaSlicer attached to its own notification (open folder, eject, cancel an upload) are not offered. Only a slice has a percentage and a known ending; other work shows a bar with no amount and is recorded as done unless its Cancel was pressed. Uploads and downloads have not been run. The tips and the object size card are not shown.
199	
200	### Agent WebView
201	
202	The production Agent interface is a separate React/TypeScript package that runs locally inside a `wxWebView`. It needs:
203	
204	- a versioned schema for commands and events;
205	- scripted mock conversations that play back the same way every time, for UI tests;
206	- messages that render as they stream in, with a scroll position that does not jump;
207	- written rules for keyboard, focus, shortcuts, clipboard, text selection, and IME (the input method used to type languages such as Chinese and Japanese);
208	- a defined state for each of these: reloading, starting up, an error in the bridge between the page and the app, and the agent being unavailable;
209	- no project state of its own. OrcaSlicer's project state stays in C++.
210	
211	#### Where logic goes: the page first
212	
213	When the same logic could live either in C++ or in a React page, put it in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++. The page is quicker to change: Vite hot-reloads it, while a C++ change means relinking a multi-gigabyte GUI library. The page's tests run in milliseconds under Vitest. The text people read is already written in the page. The text the model reads belongs there too.
214	
215	Strong reasons for C++:
216	
217	- **It reads or changes OrcaSlicer state:** presets, the model, plates, slicing, the device list. The page never owns project state (see the constraints below).
218	- **The app has to guarantee it.** This covers what a tool accepts and refuses, which tools a session may call, and what is sent to the model provider (API keys, access codes, project data). Page code can describe a limit, but only the app can enforce one.
219	- **It has to work without a page:** the MCP server, background work, tests that run without a browser.
220	- **It needs a thread the page does not have, or has to stay alive at times when the page is not.**
221	
222	The printer panel shows how this works. The app sends the page only facts: sizes, spools, which printer a card shows, and what a change altered. The page turns those facts into all of the text:
223	
224	- The page writes the model's instructions in `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` and sends them to the app with `printer_instructions`.
225	- The page writes the panel's own text in `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts`. That is the opening line and the note that goes with each tap. The opening line is sent with `printer_opening`. The note for a tap is sent inside that tap's payload.
226	
227	The app's part:
228	
229	- It decides which tools the model gets: the five printer tools and the four settings tools, the same list in every mode.
230	- It checks every tool call.
231	- It refuses a call that does not fit the conversation. Examples are adding a printer outside an Add conversation, changing a printer other than the one the conversation is about, and changing a setting on anything other than that printer.
232	- It refuses a turn that arrives with no instructions. The app has no prompt of its own to fall back on.
233	- It posts the opening line once per session.
234	- It posts the note for a tap only when the tap goes through, and limits the note to 2 KB.
235	- It still writes the notes for things only the app can find out when the tap arrives: the network printer has gone, the printer's model id is not on the list, or a save or an undo failed.
236	
237	The project assistant works the same way. Its whole system prompt is written in `AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`, and `projectInstructions.test.ts` pins it to a fixture so that a change to it is always deliberate. The page sends it with `project_instructions` on every connection. The app keeps it in the project session's profile and sends it, unchanged, as the instructions of every project request; the provider's prompt cache depends on the text staying byte-identical. The app has no default text. A turn the app starts itself before the page has sent the prompt (the first message after a file opens, or Ask AI on a print issue, while the page is still loading) waits in the reply queue and starts when the prompt arrives. The prompt lived in C++ until 2026-10-14 so that the MCP server's instructions could share part of it; they stopped sharing it on 2026-10-10. The MCP server's own instructions (`Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp`) and the request that names a conversation stay in C++: MCP has no page, and the title request is the app's own.
238	
239	Windows uses WebView2, macOS uses WKWebView, and Linux uses WebKitGTK. The way the page's files are packaged must work on all three. The prototype packed the whole page into a single local file, because WKWebView failed to load additional files referenced through `file:` URLs. Production keeps the single-file approach, and CMake now builds that file from the TypeScript/React sources.
240	
241	MCP (Model Context Protocol, which lets external AI tools call the app) and wider agent autonomy are layers that come after this one. They must go through the same typed workspace interface. They must not change who owns the 3D view.
242	
243	### Gizmo presentation
244	
245	Start with Move or Rotate. Build one reusable native controller that wraps the existing behavior:
246	
247	1. Show a compact strip of tool buttons in the upper-left corner of the Prepare canvas. The strip is a horizontal row like OrcaSlicer's own toolbar, but aligned to the left instead of centred. The strip stays put when the selection or the camera moves, because a strip attached to the object would jump every time the view orbits. `Canvas/ViewportToolStrip` draws the strip with ImGui as part of the canvas's own frame, through `GLCanvas3D::set_overlay_renderer`. On every frame it asks the gizmo manager which tool is open. The open tool's values appear below the row in `Canvas/ToolValuePanel`, lined up with the button that opened the tool.
248	2. Activate the existing native gizmo.
249	3. Keep the existing pointer dragging, snapping, and selection behavior.
250	4. Send exact typed-in numbers through `GizmoObjectManipulation`.
251	5. Keep the existing timing of undo snapshots, and the existing undo and redo.
252	6. Closing a tool only closes it. Do not invent a draft that can be thrown away. Undo stays the way to revert a change, unless the product requirements explicitly change that.
253	
254	After that, convert the remaining tools in groups that work in a similar way: Move/Rotate/Scale; Mirror/Duplicate/Place on face; Measure; Cut/Repair; Text/Emboss; painter-based tools.
255	
256	### Semantic annotations
257	
258	Semantic annotations are labels a person puts on part of a model to say what that part means, such as a face that must stay smooth. Reuse what OrcaSlicer's painting tools already do: raycasting, brush selection, clipping, showing painted facets, copying, undo, and saving into the 3MF file. Two things are not yet proven for production: labels with arbitrary meanings, and how those labels are presented to the agent. The first implementation should use two labels on one object. Before adding more labels, check that those two survive save and reload, transforms, duplication, undo and redo, and changes to the mesh's topology.
259	
260	## Non-negotiable constraints
261	
262	- Do not change slicing algorithms to make the UI easier to build.
263	- Do not replace `GLCanvas3D` or the G-code Preview.
264	- Do not reimplement geometry operations in TypeScript.
265	- Do not place WebView content over the native GL canvas.
266	- Do not keep a second copy of the project model or of the undo stack in JavaScript.
267	- Preserve 3MF projects, printer profiles, shortcuts, serialization, and cross-platform behavior.
268	- Do not try to match every stock OrcaSlicer feature when the product definition does not require it.
269	- Do not reopen the Electron or WebGL question without a new, explicit product decision backed by evidence.
270	
271	## Implementation order
272	
273	1. Write the canonical product documents, and set up the design tokens and the curated assets.
274	2. Bring the workspace interface up to production quality: the interface itself, commands that go through OrcaSlicer's own code, change observation, and tests against the real adapter.
275	3. Bring the canvas presentation API and its controller up to production quality.
276	4. Build the production shell without a compact object/plate pane.
277	5. Build the typed Agent WebView and the bridge between the page and the app.
278	6. Add the presentation controller for Move/Rotate, then convert the other groups of gizmos.
279	7. Add semantic annotations, Check print reporting, the reskinned send dialog, Monitor, calibration, and troubleshooting screens as the product definition describes them.
280	8. Add the compact object/plate pane as a separately planned task when it is prioritized.
281	
282	Older implementations and the detailed evidence are deliberately left out of this document. See [POC reference](poc-reference.md).

description: "2026-10-27 decisions for the way back from classic OrcaSlicer to the JusPrin view: banner + View-menu row, session-only, fixed wording, no tokens/boards; design + handoff docs untracked in the repo root"
metadata:

"Switch to classic view…" (Prepare overflow menu) detaches the shell in place with no way back in-session; `jusprin_shell` is read at startup and never written. On 2026-10-27 Kenneth decided the return path:

- Two fork-owned surfaces: a non-dismissible banner above the Notebook ("You're in the classic OrcaSlicer view." / button "Back to JusPrin") and a View-menu row "Switch to JusPrin view". Both re-run the shell install via a new `reattach_shell()`.
- Session-only: do not write `jusprin_shell`.
- Minimum design, default recipes only, no new token, no canvas board.
- Zero new lines in OrcaSlicer-owned files: everything reachable via `GetMenuBar()`, `MainFrame::topbar()->GetTopMenu()`, and the frame/Notebook/sizer pointers `attach_shell` already receives.

Docs: `classic-view-return-design.md` and `classic-view-return-handoff.md`, untracked in the main checkout root (see [[handoff-docs-not-committed]]).

**Why:** JusPrin is the product; classic view is a temporary escape hatch, so it should not persist, and the way back must be visible without prior knowledge.

**How to apply:** implement from the handoff; don't reopen the banner-vs-menu or persistence questions unless Kenneth does. Verify with the `--classic-switch` and `--stock` harness runs, two round trips.

Kenneth, 2026-11-06, on the wording-sweep report: "How about we have both? "Ask..." below the current one, which will be changed to opening the setting window."

**Why:** a menu item named "settings" should open settings; the chat stays available.

**How to apply:** "Printer settings…" / "Filament settings…" open Orca's settings window. A new item directly under each, "Ask AI about printer settings…" / "Ask AI about filament settings…" (my wording, following [[ai-is-the-feature-name]]), opens the chat. He was choosing among the names the UI used then: "the Agent" (chat, Preferences › Agent), "AI agent" (welcome), "Ask AI" (print issue bubble), "the assistant" (issue chat). I had recommended "the agent"; he overruled it.

result.output:
# Local autosave and version history

JusPrin saves authored projects in the application data directory under
`jusprin/projects/<project-id>/`. The project ID is independent of the source
filename. Opening an external 3MF or model imports it into a managed draft;
autosave never overwrites the source. **Saved** means the printable
project checkpoint and the current JusPrin document are durable. A 3MF is written
to a user-selected path only through **Export project 3MF…**. A copied 3MF does
not include local versions, conversations, or attachments.

The project header's actions menu exposes the save state, version history,
recent local projects, and export. Version history restores an earlier model
and its effective project settings. The native window title shows the managed
project name and the same save state as the header. Orca's dirty asterisk
does not represent whether the local project has been saved. Before restoring,
JusPrin saves and pins
the current version, then records the restore as a new version, so the prior
state remains available. Each older timestamp has a separate Restore button;
clicking the timestamp does nothing, and Restore asks for confirmation. Document
edits do not add versions.
Conversations with each chat's intent and plan, audit, and completed print
records remain in the current document; restoring a model marks the active
chat's plan for reassessment. Region descriptions follow the model: each
version records the list it was saved with, and restoring it brings that list
back. Restoring a model does not undo physical prints or change
global printer facts. Agent
mutations save and pin their actual
before-state, then link an after-version and outcome in an operation record.

## Storage and recovery contract

The restoration rules above describe ordinary Version history. **Restore and
resume** is a separate chat transition. Each chat owns its print's purpose and
plan; the project's current ones are the active chat's. A chat's checkpoint
holds a model-version reference and a structured setup summary of the moment
it was left. Browsing an older chat does not change the working project.
Resuming it saves and pins the outgoing state, restores the model with its
region descriptions, and activates that chat, whose intent and plan never left
it, only after the new document is durable. Other conversations, audit and print
records, and global printer facts remain. This does not add a full project-
written is such a failure: the version list is read once when the project
opens and then kept in memory, so the Agent page and Version history keep
working from it while every save is refused, and saving resumes on the next
retry once the folder is available again. Home and Recent projects list
projects by reading the projects folder. A project whose folder cannot be
read is left out of the list, like a damaged one. If the projects folder
itself cannot be read, Home says the projects couldn't be loaded instead of
showing an empty gallery, and keeps reading the folder while it is on
screen, so the projects reappear once the folder is readable; the header's
Recent projects menu says they couldn't be loaded. Opening a file while the
projects folder cannot be read stops before anything is replaced, because
whether the file was opened before cannot be told: a person is told so, and
the Agent's `project_open` fails with `local_save_failed` saying why. Project replacement is blocked until the live
state is saved. Explicit export validates a temporary 3MF before replacing
its destination.

Older projects may still contain `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json`. On first adoption, JusPrin reads that state and copies its
attachments to the managed store; it does not delete the old source. Once a
managed version exists, local state is authoritative. Reopening a copied
external 3MF with an already managed identity forks a new project identity.
When a file opened as a project matches a saved project, JusPrin asks whether
to create another project or open the existing one directly. A project
remembers the file it was opened from (`openedFrom`) and that file's MD5 then
(`openedDigest`) in each version manifest: a .3mf from its project path, a model
file the agent's `project_open` opened as a new project from the path it gave.
Every way a person opens a .3mf asks, because the check sits in
`Plater::load_project` (File > Open Project, recent files, Finder, Home's
Open…, drops on Home and on the Prepare canvas); the
agent's `project_open` returns the question as `opened_before` and takes the
answer as `openedBefore`. A file whose MD5 differs is a likely new export, so
the question says so and defaults to a new project; otherwise it defaults to
the saved one. Adding a file to the open project (Add model…, File > Import,
the agent's `object_import`) never asks. If several
projects match, it continues the current one when it came from that file;
otherwise it opens the most recently updated match. Which ways in open a file
as a new project and which add to the open one is decided in
[Opening and importing files](architecture.md#opening-and-importing-files).
The project document has one schema version and no migration (the project is
not live yet): a document of any other version, like a corrupt one, is
replaced by a fresh document. The local store reads only its current index,
manifest and current-document formats.
Recent projects appear on Home and in the header menu. Selecting one
opens its managed version even when its imported source file has been removed.
Nothing reopens on startup: the app starts on Home with a blank project behind
it, and a saved project opens only when the person picks it.

## Chosen defaults and limits

- The controller checks a lightweight native state signature every 2 seconds
  and waits 1.5 seconds after an observed model edit before starting a background
  model save. Document changes use the coalesced state write described above;

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them
into the strip at construction. The Phase 1 production shell reached a
19-added-line upstream footprint this way where the POC's reparenting shell
needed edits across eight upstream files.

The same measurement gives the rule for every fork-owned screen that comes
after the shell. OrcaSlicer's surfaces (the stock homepage, Prepare, Preview,
Monitor, the settings tabs) stay inside the Notebook, because their
correctness depends on it. Fork-owned surfaces (the header, the Agent pane,
Home, and whatever follows) live outside it, as siblings of the Notebook in a
fork-owned sizer, shown and hidden by the shell. The shell *reads* the
Notebook's selection to decide what to show and *never edits its page list*:
no `RemovePage`, `InsertPage`, or reparenting of a stock page. Removing or
replacing a page hands the fork the meaning of that index. Upstream keeps
addressing it by number — `tpHome` as a dialog parent, the target of
`EVT_LOAD_URL`, the tab `post_init` returns to — and every one of those lands
on the fork's widget with no conflict and no error. If a fork surface truly
must be a page, append it last, where no upstream code addresses it.

Navigation between screens stays a Notebook selection change even when the
screen being left is fork-owned. Menu and shortcut enabling, undo and redo
availability, and slice-status updates all read `GetSelection()`, so the
selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.
Showing Prepare any other way leaves those predicates answering for the wrong
page, silently.

content.text:
Most of the menu bar no longer fits JusPrin. Every item is still OrcaSlicer's, except for three small changes JusPrin made. Some items work against autosave, some do nothing while JusPrin's shell is on, and the screens JusPrin added have no menu items at all.

**JusPrin's goal (from `agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`).** The person says what is physically true, what the object means and what result they want. The AI picks the technical settings, and the person checks the plan and stays in control of the printer. Projects autosave into JusPrin's own store, and a 3MF is only written to a folder the person picks through "Export project 3MF…".

**What JusPrin already changed.** It added File › Import › Import from OrcaSlicer…. It hides OrcaSlicer's Calibration menu while the shell is on. In classic view it adds a "Switch to JusPrin view" row to View. The last two are done from JusPrin's own code, so no OrcaSlicer file was edited.

**Items that work against JusPrin**
- **Save Project (Cmd+S).** When JusPrin opens a 3MF, it gives OrcaSlicer the original file's path as the project path. OrcaSlicer's Save writes to that path without asking. So, as far as I can tell from the code, opening `~/Downloads/bracket.3mf` and pressing Cmd+S overwrites the downloaded file, which the autosave doc promises never happens. I haven't tried this in the app.
- **File › Recent files** is OrcaSlicer's list of file paths. Home and the header menu list JusPrin's saved projects instead.
- **Help › Setup Wizard** opens OrcaSlicer's wizard with its long printer and filament lists. The product definition says to replace exactly that with finding the printer and a short confirmation, and JusPrin's first-run screens already do that.
- **Help › Check for Updates** asks OrcaSlicer's update server. JusPrin's version number is in OrcaSlicer's format (02.06.00.51), so I'd expect it to be compared with OrcaSlicer's releases. I haven't tried this either.

**Items that do nothing while the shell is on**
- **New Window:** JusPrin forces a single running instance, so this item stays greyed out.
- **Show G-code Window:** it only works on OrcaSlicer's Preview tab, which the shell never shows.
- **Reset Window Layout:** it needs OrcaSlicer's sidebar, which the shell turns off.
- **Show Tip of the Day:** the shell doesn't draw the tips.
- **Sync Presets:** it needs an OrcaCloud sign-in, and I found nowhere in JusPrin to sign in to OrcaCloud.

**What's missing.** There is no menu item for Home, for showing or hiding the Plates pane or the AI panel, or for Slice, Check print and Print. The same goes for Ask AI, adding a printer, printer and filament settings, Version history and "Export project 3MF…".

**What I propose (nothing here is agreed yet)**
- **File:** New Project, Open…, and Open Recent showing JusPrin's projects. Then Version History…, Import, and Export with JusPrin's "Project 3MF…" first, followed by OrcaSlicer's G-code and mesh exports. Drop New Window and Sync Presets.
- **Edit:** keep it as it is.
- **View:** Home, then Show Plates pane and Show AI panel. Keep the camera views and the display options for the 3D view. Add "Switch to classic view…". Drop the G-code window and Reset Window Layout items.
- **Print (new menu):** Slice plate (Cmd+R, OrcaSlicer's existing shortcut), Slice all, Check print, Print…, Export G-code.
- **Printer (new menu):** Add printer…, Printer settings…, Ask AI about printer settings…, Filament settings…, Ask AI about filament settings…, Calibrate…. These are the same items as the header's printer menu.
- **Help:** Ask AI…, Keyboard Shortcuts, Report a problem…, Show Configuration Folder, Troubleshoot Center, Network Test. Drop Setup Wizard and Tip of the Day.

**How I'd build it.** I'd use the same method JusPrin already uses to hide Calibration. JusPrin's own code edits the finished menu bar when the shell starts and puts it back for classic view, so `MainFrame.cpp` stays as it is. One catch: that code finds menus by their translated names. It should stop with an error if a name isn't found, as the Calibration code does, so a rename upstream fails loudly instead of quietly.

**Decision needed: what Cmd+S should do.** This is your call because it changes a habit every slicer user has, and it decides what "saved" means in JusPrin. One option is to remove Save and Save As and let Cmd+S do nothing. That is honest about autosave, but people will press it and see nothing happen. The second option is to make Cmd+S save a pinned version right away, like Pages on macOS, and turn Save As into "Export project 3MF…". This is a little more work, because versions can already be pinned but not from a shortcut. The third option is to keep OrcaSlicer's behaviour, which may overwrite the downloaded file. My pick is the second one. Which do you want?

**Decision needed: Check for Updates.** This is your call because it depends on whether JusPrin has its own release feed, and I couldn't find one. One option is to hide the item until there is a feed, which costs nothing. The other is to point it at a JusPrin feed now, which first needs that feed on the server. My pick is to hide it for now. Which do you prefer?

> Printer (new menu): Add printer…, Printer settings…, Ask AI about printer settings…, Filament settings…, Ask AI about filament settings…, Calibrate…. These are the same items as the header’s printer menu.

I like this suggestion. But I also have a question: these should be hidden when the user is on the home screen or no project is open, right? It is a common practice to have a top-level menu that works only for certain screens, but not others? actually I think we should go back to the first principles and ask for ourselves what should belong to the menu. The Apple guidance is clear: when a menu action isn't available, the item should stay in the menu and be disabled. The current Apple HIG menu bar page says so directly, and the cited text is the source's own wording, so I've paraphrased around it. It recommends disabling an unavailable action rather than removing it from the menu.

Supporting context:
- Mac users have long been taught to expect every command in the menu bar. One Macworld piece calls the rule thou shalt not hide menu items from the user, and argues that users rely on the menu bar as the single place to find commands.
- A cocoa-dev thread from 2009 says that Apple's guidelines are against keeping users from seeing submenus, even when everything inside is disabled. That is a forum post, not an official source.
- Apple's own HIG-era guidance on dimmed items is quoted in a 2011 LibreOffice thread. It says an unavailable item should appear dimmed (gray) in the menu, rather than disappear.
- For top-level menus, a Stack Overflow answer notes that a menu's title stays visible even when every command inside is dimmed, and that users should always be able to view a menu's contents, whether or not they are currently available.

Note: the search surfaced only the current HIG page's "best practices" line directly. The other sources are secondary or old, so check the live HIG page before relying on any of them for a specific wording.

On a Mac or an iPad, the menu bar at the top of the screen displays the top-level menus in your app or game.

## Discussion

![A stylized representation of the macOS menu bar displaying a selected menu. The image is tinted red to subtly reflect the red in the original six-color Apple logo.](images/com.apple.HIG/components-the-menu-bar-intro~dark@2x.png)

Mac users are very familiar with the macOS menu bar, and they rely on it to help them learn what an app does and find the commands they need. To help your app or game feel at home in macOS, it’s essential to provide a consistent menu bar experience.

Menu bar menus on iPad are similar to those on Mac, appearing in the same order and with familiar sets of menu items. When you adopt the menu structure that people expect from their experience on Mac, it helps them immediately understand and take advantage of the menu bar on iPad as well.

Keyboard shortcuts in iPadOS use the same patterns as in macOS. For guidance, see [Standard keyboard shortcuts](/design/Human-Interface-Guidelines/keyboards#Standard-keyboard-shortcuts).

![An illustration of an app window on iPad, with its menu bar appearing at the top of the screen and the Edit menu open.](images/com.apple.HIG/menu-bar-ipad-overview~dark@2x.png)

Menus in the menu bar share most of the appearance and behavior characteristics that all menu types have. To learn about menus in general — and how to organize and label menu items — see [Menus](/design/Human-Interface-Guidelines/menus).

## Anatomy

When present in the menu bar, the following menus appear in the order listed below.

- *YourAppName* (you supply a short version of your app’s name for this menu’s title)
- File
- Edit
- Format
- View

The search returned nothing on Onshape, so this covers Fusion 360 only. The results are mostly Autodesk community forum posts, and some are old, so Autodesk's current documentation may differ.

- **Ctrl+S creates a cloud version.** Autodesk staff have said Ctrl+S saves to the cloud and increments the version number, which is why users often get prompted for a version description whenever they click Save or press Ctrl+S, which creates a cloud version.
- **Ctrl+Shift+S makes a local recovery save.** Staff described this as a checkpoint kept on the machine that does not create a version. Ctrl+Shift+S was added in a November update. It forces a local recovery save, which protects against a crash, and it does not create a version. Another user noted it only saves a recovery file and does not save to the cloud.
- **Autosave is interval-based.** Users note that the autosave or automatic versioning interval can be set in Preferences, with 15 minutes as the minimum in one older thread, while another user reported a 5-minute recovery interval setting. Autosave runs on a timer, so it can miss work if a session crashes before the next save, and one user reported that if you are working non-stop, the autosave never gets a chance to save.
- **Known friction.** Users have complained that the version-description dialog can interrupt a quick Ctrl+S, and that it can appear right before a crash.

13c06c3ff3 2026-10-23 Kenneth Jiang
Publish JusPrin's own releases, packaged as JusPrin

A hand-started workflow builds JusPrin and uploads it to a draft GitHub
release; publishing stays a manual click on the Releases page.

- jusprin_release.yml (Run workflow, or a push to jusprin-release/*)
  builds Windows x64, macOS universal and Linux x64 from one commit and
  uploads the installer, portable zip, disk image, AppImage and
  SHA256SUMS.txt to a draft tagged jusprin/v<version>. The version is
  the one in Version.hpp. Packaging/release.mjs (with tests) refuses a
  version that is already released, below the latest release, or whose
  tag exists: the repo still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.0.0..v2.3.1 tags,
  and a published draft takes an existing tag's commit. The notes come
  from Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md. Only the release publisher
  may run it; macOS signing runs only when asked for, with JusPrin 1.x's
  Apple secrets; an unsigned draft says so in its title.
- The build reuses OrcaSlicer's build_deps.yml (build-deps-only), its
  cache key and its build scripts. build_orca.yml can't be reused: its
  Linux step expects OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a build
  with JusPrin's app key never writes. No OrcaSlicer workflow is changed.
- Packaging/packaging.cmake gives the Windows installer JusPrin's name,
  publisher (Obico), version, install folder, shortcuts, icon and
  uninstall key "JusPrin" (JusPrin 1.x's, so 2.x replaces 1.x). Before,
  the installer was OrcaSlicer's and, with uninstall-before-install on,
  would have removed a real OrcaSlicer. The macOS app becomes JusPrin.app
  (io.obico.jusprin) and the AppImage gets JusPrin's desktop entry.
- Built-in profiles now change only with a JusPrin release: attach_shell()
  turns off sync_system_preset, and Preferences > Updates says so instead
  of offering a checkbox. PresetUpdater::check_vendor_update() now obeys
  that preference and stealth mode, as the startup check does; before, it
  asked check-version.orcaslicer.com whenever the printer changed to
  another maker's.

OrcaSlicer-owned lines: one include added to CMakeLists.txt before
include(CPack); three lines added at the top of
PresetUpdater::check_vendor_update(). Nothing upstream is deleted or
rewritten. Simulated against upstream/main 76ddcab0ab (base 3ffb9585d2):
neither file conflicts, and the conflict list is the same as without
these changes. Upstream main gates online profile updates behind
enable_ota (default off); at that rebase the three lines may conflict
with upstream's rework of check_vendor_update(), and dropping them is
then correct.

platform and made the draft; a local Windows build's installer script
names JusPrin 2.0.0 and only the JusPrin uninstall key.

input.recap: Nothing in the code has changed. The researched rules say a menu is the full list of the app's commands. Menus never hide by screen: an item is greyed out while it can't run and removed only if it can never run. JusPrin's own update check already exists, but no agent doc mentions it.
input.ask: Shall I add a short note on releases and the update check to the agent docs?

content.text:
Short answers first. The new Print and Printer menus should stay on the menu bar on every screen, Home included. When an item can't run, it is greyed out, not hidden. Apps that autosave mostly keep Cmd+S and use it to save a version. And I was wrong last time: JusPrin's own update check is already built. Nothing in the agent docs says so, which is why I missed it.

## What belongs in the menu

Apple's guidelines for the Mac menu bar ([The menu bar](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/the-menu-bar)) and the older Windows and KDE guidance agree on a few rules:

1. **The menu bar lists every command the app has.** Apple says to list a command there "even when commands are available elsewhere in your app", including rarely used and advanced ones. People look there to learn what the app can do, and it is how keyboard and accessibility users reach those commands. For JusPrin, this means Version history, Export project 3MF, Ask AI, Switch to classic view and the printer commands belong in menus. Today they exist only in the header and on Home.
2. **The same menus are shown on every screen.** Apple says to "always show the same set of menu items" and to disable an item rather than hide it. So someone on Home opens Print, sees "Slice plate" greyed out, and learns that it exists for when a model is open.
3. **An item is removed only when it can never run in this app.** The older Microsoft guidance, [Raymond Chen](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20040514-00/?p=39343) and the [KDE guidelines](https://develop.kde.org/hig/components/navigation/menubar) all draw the line there. If the person can make an item work, grey it out. If they never can, remove it, or they will hunt for a way to switch it on. New Window and Show G-code Window fail this test while JusPrin's shell is on, so they go. Slice passes it, so it stays and is greyed out.
4. **Standard menus come in the standard order, with their usual shortcuts.** On the Mac the order is the app menu, File, Edit, View, then the app's own menus, then Window and Help. The app's own menus should follow how its objects nest, the way Mail has Mailbox, then Message, then Format.
5. **Show and hide items name what they will do now.** "Hide AI Panel" while the panel is open, "Show AI Panel" while it is closed.
6. **The menu bar is not a dumping ground.** Every command still needs a home in the app's own screens, because the menu bar is hidden in full screen.

From these, here is my proposal. Print and Printer stay on the menu bar on Home too. Under Print, Slice plate, Check print, Print… and Export G-code are greyed out until the plate has something to slice. Behind Home there is always a blank project, so "no project open" never really happens. The Printer items (Add printer, the settings windows, Ask AI about them, Calibrate) are about printers, not projects, so they work from Home as they are. One gap I haven't checked: Apple says to provide a Window menu even when the app has only one window, and I don't know whether wxWidgets adds one.

## How apps that autosave handle Cmd+S

- **Mac document apps** (Pages, TextEdit, Keynote) save on their own as you work. They still keep File › Save on Cmd+S, which adds the current state to the version history ([Eclectic Light](https://eclecticlight.co/2025/04/29/document-versioning-unused-power-in-macos/)). Save As becomes **Duplicate** (Cmd+Shift+S). **Revert To ▸ Browse All Versions** opens the history ([MacSales](https://eshop.macsales.com/blog/47415-auto-save-and-versions-an-often-overlooked-mac-feature/)). Apple prefers Duplicate to Save As and Export because those "don't clarify the relationship between the original file and the new one". Apple keeps Export for formats the app doesn't normally use.
- **Fusion 360** autosaves for crash recovery. Its Ctrl+S saves a new cloud version, and Ctrl+Shift+S makes a local recovery save ([Autodesk forum](https://forums.autodesk.com/t5/fusion-support-forum/trick-to-save-design-without-advancing-version-number/m-p/9323483)).
- **Figma** saves every change at once and puts "Save to version history" on Cmd+Option+S ([Figma help](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038006754)). I couldn't confirm what a plain Cmd+S does there.

I found no app that leaves Cmd+S doing nothing. So the research supports the option I picked last time. Cmd+S would save and pin a version, and Version History would sit in the File menu.

**Decision needed: what replaces Save As.** Apple's answer is Duplicate, which copies the project as a new JusPrin project. JusPrin can't do that today. Pinning a version already exists inside the autosave code, but copying a project would be new work. The cheaper option is to put "Export project 3MF…" on Cmd+Shift+S. That already works, but it writes a file outside JusPrin rather than a new project, which is exactly the confusion Apple warns about. My pick is to put Export on Cmd+Shift+S now and add Duplicate when someone asks for it. Do you agree?

## The update check: it is built

JusPrin's update check went in on 2026-10-23 in two commits:
- `80ed1692ff` added the check itself, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/`. It reads JusPrin's GitHub releases at startup and once a day, and shows the result in Preferences › Updates with Download and Skip this version.
- `13c06c3ff3` added the release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`. It builds every platform into a draft release that you publish by hand.

OrcaSlicer's check never runs. A JusPrin line in OrcaSlicer's `GUI_App.cpp` (`21d1e268ba`) passes it to JusPrin's check, including Help › Check for Updates, which then opens Preferences › Updates. So the item is fine as it is. Last time I read the URL further down that function and missed the hand-over at its top.

**Why it isn't documented:** both commits explain it in their commit messages, code comments and the workflow file's header, and neither changed `agent-docs`. Nothing in AGENTS.md asks for a doc when a feature lands. I couldn't find the session where you discussed it: searching this app's past sessions for the update and release words turned up nothing.

**Should it be documented?** Yes, briefly. It is not something you build and forget, for three reasons:
- Releasing is a manual routine someone repeats. They set the version in `Version.hpp`, write the notes file, run the workflow and publish the draft. OrcaSlicer's old v2.x tags in the repo are a trap the workflow guards against.
- The hand-over line lives in an OrcaSlicer file, so a future rebase has to carry it.
- I just got it wrong because the docs are silent.

A few lines pointing at those files would be enough.
Not now

OK, I'll leave the agent docs as they are. The Cmd+S overwrite I found by reading the code also hasn't been tried in the app. Whenever you want, I can reproduce it, add the release note, or build any of the menu changes.

Microsoft's guidance supports the core of your premise, with one caveat: "Save a Copy" doesn't replace Save As everywhere, and Ctrl+S's role depends on the file's location.

- **Cloud files with AutoSave on:** Microsoft's support page says that when AutoSave is on, changes are continually written to the original file, so Microsoft recommends using File > Save a Copy before editing if you want the changes to go only to the copy. When AutoSave is on, your changes are continually saved to the original. So we recommend using File > Save a Copy before you make any changes if you want your changes to apply to the copy and not the original.
- **Where the command appears:** Save As isn't on the File menu when you open a document from OneDrive, OneDrive for Business or SharePoint Online. In these cases, the Save a Copy command appears on the File menu instead.
- **Ctrl+S:** Microsoft's page says you can still save manually with Ctrl+S, but it frames that in the context of AutoSave being off. And, of course, you can always save manually the way you always have, by either pressing CTRL+S, clicking the Save button, or going to File > Save. Under AutoSave, Ctrl+S is not the mechanism that writes your changes.
- **Local files:** AutoSave is not available when working with local files. Traditional Save As still applies there, and AutoRecover is only a crash-recovery safety net, not a real save. AutoRecover is NOT a full save, instead it saves a record of recent changes to a separate location.

Some third-party sites (WPS, Alibaba Office) describe the same behavior and suggest turning AutoSave off to restore classic Save As. Microsoft's own page is the more authoritative source, so I'd rely on it first.
